directions: Drag only the relevant data into your Research Journal for the study's Objective.

blocks.text: Thornmere Lake is a large inland lake made up of four basins. For decades its fish stocks have supported a healthy recreational fishery, managed by the regional lake authority and fished by anglers from across the region.

However, [[cormorant_intro]], a colony of Slate-crested Cormorants settled on the lake, and further colonies have since formed in every basin. The cormorants feed on the lake's fish, and anglers have reported falling catches in each basin since.
Your team of ecologists has been asked to assess the lake authority's plan to protect the fish stocks.

The lake authority's plan has two measures. A cull will [[plan_cull]]. Bird-scaring devices along the shore will [[plan_devices]]. Both measures will be [[plan_timing]]. The devices cost [[plan_cost]], and the plan will be [[plan_review]]. A catch-and-release rule for Bream was also discussed but [[plan_release]].
To judge the plan, your team surveyed the four fish species most often taken by Slate-crested Cormorants. Their stocks, split across the four basins of Thornmere Lake, are as follows:

objective_line.label: Objective
objective_line.text: Review the data and determine whether the lake authority's plan will meet its target of cutting the yearly fish loss in Linden Bay and Coldwater Arm by at least 25%.
objective_line.needed_for: Every question: it defines which two basins matter; Question 4 and the Report: the 25% target

plan_cull.label: The cull
plan_cull.text: remove 4 birds from every colony of more than 10 birds
plan_cull.needed_for: Question 3: the cull applies only where the colony is large enough

plan_devices.label: Bird-scaring devices
plan_devices.text: cut the feeding rate of a colony by 20%

plan_timing.label: Timing of the plan
plan_timing.text: in place for the whole of next year
plan_timing.needed_for: Question 3: both measures apply to the full 325 days

plan_release.label: Catch-and-release proposal
plan_release.text: is not part of the plan

other_prey_diet.label: Other fish species' contribution toward Slate-crested Cormorant diets
other_prey_diet.text: a very small share of their diet
other_prey_diet.needed_for: Questions 2 and 3: the four surveyed species are the whole catch

feeding_rate_def.label: Definition of feeding rate
feeding_rate_def.text: number of the four surveyed fish species taken per day per cormorant

feeding_behavior.label: Slate-crested Cormorant feeding behavior
feeding_behavior.text: the four species are taken in proportion to their stock

year_days.label: Feeding rate over the year
year_days.text: Once calculated, the feeding rate is expected to remain constant for the 325 days a year that the cormorants spend on the lake

additional_data_1.label: Additional data #1
additional_data_1.text: Ashby Reach: 2 birds left the colony

additional_data_4.label: Additional data #4
additional_data_4.text: Linden Bay: one more bird found in the colony than first counted
additional_data_4.needed_for: Questions 1, 2 and 3: the corrected colony size

additional_data_6.label: Additional data #6
additional_data_6.text: Heron Shallows: 3 more birds joined the colony

ex2_2_2.label: Total fish taken in Linden Bay

ex2_3_2.label: Total fish taken in Coldwater Arm

explanation: Only the two basins named in the objective, Linden Bay and Coldwater Arm, matter, so everything about Ashby Reach and Heron Shallows is a distractor. So are the year the cormorants arrived, the cost and review of the plan, the catch-and-release proposal (it is not part of the plan), the assumption that the species are taken in proportion to their stock (no question uses it), and the feeding rates printed in Exhibit 2 (the new rate is worked out from the totals, and nothing compares it with the old one). The three plan items are needed for Question 3, and the colony sizes are used three times: for the rate, for the yearly catch, and for the cull.
